import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def task_func(df, x_column, y_column):
    """
    Draw a scatter plot for the specified columns from a pandas DataFrame,
    fit a linear regression model, and overlay the predicted regression line.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pandas.DataFrame
        Input data.
    x_column : str
        Name of the column to use for the x-axis.
    y_column : str
        Name of the column to use for the y-axis.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes
        The Axes object containing the scatter plot and regression line.
    """
    if x_column not in df.columns or y_column not in df.columns:
        raise KeyError("Both x_column and y_column must exist in the DataFrame.")

    data = df[[x_column, y_column]].dropna()
    if data.empty:
        raise ValueError("No valid rows remain after dropping missing values.")

    x = pd.to_numeric(data[x_column], errors="raise").to_numpy().reshape(-1, 1)
    y = pd.to_numeric(data[y_column], errors="raise").to_numpy()

    finite_mask = np.isfinite(x[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(y)
    x = x[finite_mask]
    y = y[finite_mask]

    if x.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("No finite numeric data available for regression.")

    model = LinearRegression()
    model.fit(x, y)

    x_min = float(np.min(x))
    x_max = float(np.max(x))
    line_x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, 200).reshape(-1, 1)
    line_y = model.predict(line_x)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.scatter(x[:, 0], y, alpha=0.7, label="Data")
    ax.plot(line_x[:, 0], line_y, color="red", linewidth=2, label="Regression line")
    ax.set_xlabel(x_column)
    ax.set_ylabel(y_column)
    ax.legend()

    return ax
